character.lede: A modern barn cluster pairs a brick lounge gable with a taller charcoal curtain-wall gable under a black roof. A black-tile court with a round plunge pool sits below the dining deck.

spots.line: A sofa, two barrel chairs and a trunk table fill the library lounge.
A standing desk and a bookshelf make a workspace on the landing.
A tuxedo sofa, two slipper chairs and a bookshelf fill the loft.

facts.style: Modern barn cluster: a brick lounge gable and a taller charcoal curtain-wall gable, each glazed to the apex under a solid black roof, a set-back vertical-timber entry wing, a brick chimney, cypresses, a stone-edged gravel path, and a black-tile court with a round plunge pool below a dining deck

character.truths: The Core sits on a credenza in the Library Lounge. There is no television and no kitchen island. Noam works at a standing desk on the upper landing. Plunge pool in a black-tile court below a dining deck.

signatureStack.name: HomeBox
signatureStack.seed: The oven warranty turns up in a HomeBox record with the receipt photo, a label and a shelf.
signatureStack.line: HomeBox gives every box in the loft and garage a label, a place and a note about what is inside.

signatureStack.name: InfluxDB 2
signatureStack.seed: Noam writes the rover's wheel readings into InfluxDB 2 and plots a run against the drift.
signatureStack.line: InfluxDB 2 keeps the greenhouse and garden sensor readings in one time-series store.

signatureStack.name: JupyterLab
signatureStack.seed: Noam finds why the rover drifts left in a JupyterLab notebook of its wheel readings.
signatureStack.line: JupyterLab runs the statistics homework as a notebook on the Core.

signatureStack.name: Pingvin Share
signatureStack.seed: A big video leaves the laptop as a Pingvin Share link that opens on any phone at home and expires after a day.
signatureStack.line: Pingvin Share makes a link for a big file that someone in the house opens.

signatureStack.name: draw.io
signatureStack.seed: Noam draws the rover's wiring in draw.io and saves the diagram as a file on his own machine.
signatureStack.line: draw.io draws the flow chart and saves the file where the person chooses.

signatureStack.name: CryptPad
signatureStack.seed: The studio drafts the project brief in a CryptPad document, and each edit appears as it is typed.
signatureStack.line: CryptPad opens a shared pad and a kanban board that two people edit together at home.

signatureStack.name: Baikal
signatureStack.seed: Ruth makes room for a visitor on the calendar that Baikal serves from the Core to both phones.
signatureStack.line: Baikal serves the household calendar from the Core, and the calendar app on each phone reads it at home.

signatureStack.name: mStream
signatureStack.seed: The old CDs play again from the family's own music folder through the lounge speaker with mStream.
signatureStack.line: mStream plays a record collection, digitised years ago, through the living-room speaker.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

nextcloud: [note] The Hub onboarding wizard offers Nextcloud as a recommended app.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
gitea: [note] Gitea Mirror is a different listing (it copies GitHub repositories into Gitea). Name only Gitea. Forgejo does the same job; name one Git host per household.
[note] The listing mentions Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing mentions Actions CI; no runner ships: never show a CI run.
Gitea Mirror is a different app.
mstream: Description says "from anywhere", "completely private" and "no data collection": absolute and remote claims, paraphrase
pi-hole: [claims] Network-wide blocking at DNS. Do not call it parental control or promise safety.
Blocks ad, tracker and bad domains at DNS: not parental control and no promise of safety
Unblocked lookups are forwarded to an upstream resolver (the upstream demo dashboard lists a public DNS, dns.google), so a DNS provider still sees them and it is not offline
Overlaps AdGuard Home: one per household
espocrm: [note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
n8n: [licence] Fair-code licence, not open source. Say "source-available"; do not say "open source".
[note] An n8n MCP entry exists for agents.
Fair-code licence: say source-available, never open source.
Public URL setting is for webhooks; leave off the scene.
Listing says full control over data: connectors to cloud services still pass data to them.
vaultwarden: [note] Bitwarden-compatible server, unofficial. Do not say "Bitwarden".
stirling-pdf: QA screenshot is a sign-in wall that prints default credentials
already in the persona pool: share cap risk
homehub: No passwords: a "Select your user" box offers every name including Administrator (anyone on the network can pick one)
Extras bundled: recipes, expiry tracker, link shortener, PDF compressor, QR generator
homebox: [note] Barcode and Open Food Facts lookups call outside services.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Analytics are switched off in the manifest (good)
baikal: Whoever opens the app first runs the install wizard and sets the admin password
Overlaps Radicale and Nextcloud calendars: one calendar server per household
jupyterlab: [note] One password set at install. The notebook kernel runs the code on the Core; installing a Python package reaches the internet.

[claims] Neither the manifest, the live store nor the Portal alternatives table (origin/main) names anything it replaces, so there is no replaces chip. The CI-Common campaign reference says MATLAB or RStudio, from a sour
QA screenshot is the token and password wall: reject.
Logo file shows only the orange arcs, not the Jupyter wordmark.
penpot: Five containers (frontend, backend, exporter, Postgres, Redis).
QA screenshot is the log-in page: reject.
Listing images show community library tiles: marketing.
hortusfox: Do not say it keeps plants alive
Plant health alerts and a public gallery exist: keep the gallery off in a story
photoview: [cloud-link] Map view uses a Mapbox token you can add. Leave it off for a fully local gallery.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Public sharing links need inbound reach: keep out of stories
Face recognition is a feature, not a claim to amplify
influxdb2: QA screenshot is the welcome page.
Needs something writing to it (Home Assistant or sensors).
drawio: Stateless: diagrams live in the browser or as .drawio files on the person's own device. The Core serves the editor only, so never say the diagram sits on the Core.
Listing says nothing else phones home: leave it.
QA screenshot is a blank editor.
aider: [cloud-link] The Hub injects its own model endpoint, so it needs no cloud key. A model override field can point it at another OpenAI-compatible endpoint; leave it on the Hub model. A coding agent is private only on the C
[claims] Never claim parity with a hosted coding model and never a speed figure. Every edit is a git commit, which is the approval step: the person reviews and can undo it with git.
[note] The browser interface is marked experimental upstream. Do not call it finished.
[note] Added 2026-10-15 for the builder archetype: the old cloud-or-developer exclusion lumped it with apps that need cloud keys; this one is wired to the local model.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
syncthing: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
cryptpad: Listing says "end-to-end encrypted": banned wording (f-security-guarantee), do not repeat
Collaboration with people outside the home needs outside reach
solidtime: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
listing mentions invoices: say nothing about billing or tax
akaunting: [claims] Bookkeeping tool. No accounting, tax or legal advice.
marketplace: Source-available (Business Source License). Seafile and others carry umbrel strings: the admin email default is a placeholder address on umbrel.local.
enclosed: Listing and the app's own header say "private and secure notes" and "server never sees plaintext": do not repeat
Overlaps Cryptgeon and PrivateBin: one per household
Notes can carry an optional note password and an expiry
invoice-ninja: [cloud-link] Taking card payments needs a payment provider. Say invoicing, not payment processing.
pingvin-share: [public-access] Recipients outside your home network need to reach your Core.
public-access for anyone outside the house

caveats: QA screenshot is the welcome page.
